title: Batch formation silence and fairness restoration report
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: A cluster-wide regression introduced intermittent 'batch formation silence' on continuous-batcher hosts during peak load. Silence led to sudden tail-latency spikes for small requests and an observed unfairness where long-lived high-throughput tenants monopolized batch slots. This ticket captures investigation, immediate mitigations, and planned engineering work to restore fair-share behavior and prevent recurrence.
impact: Incidents observed across 3 regions over two 45-minute windows on 2026-02-28. 12% of production requests experienced >5x tail-latency increase; customer error budgets were impacted for two mid-market customers (support tickets opened). No data loss. Intermittent but reproducible under synthetic load patterns.
timeline: 2026-02-28T09:12: operator pager triggered by latency SLI alert; 09:15 initial mitigation (degraded to conservative batch timer) applied via autoscaler policy; 09:40 pattern reappeared in second wave; 10:05 rolling restart of batcher process on affected hosts; 10:22 observed normalization. Post-incident analysis started 2026-03-01. Reproduction harness run 2026-03-03 confirmed threshold drift under mixed-size request distributions.
root_cause: A recent heuristic change (runtime commit abc123) relaxed the batch-formation gating threshold to reduce average latency for large sequences. Under skewed arrival patterns with many high-throughput long requests, this change allowed a small number of long requests to hold the batch window open and starve small request flows. Additional interaction with a recently-introduced KV cache eviction policy caused unexpected lock contention, amplifying silent windows when eviction coincided with an overloaded I/O scheduler.
mitigation: Immediate: revert heuristic tweak on 2026-02-28 to restore previous gating behavior; enable conservative batch timers for tenant classes 'standard' and below; apply temporary KV cache eviction backoff to avoid synchronized evictions. Long-term: implement preemptible fast-path for small requests and fair-share slot accounting (see action items).
action_items: ENG-520315: Implement fair-share slot accounting in continuous-batcher so each tenant gets proportional batch slot allocation (owner: Liam Chen, estimate: 5, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-520316: Add a fast-path that short-circuits the batch window for requests below configured size/latency thresholds (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-520317: Instrument per-tenant batch holding time and expose dashboard for real-time alerts (owner: Omar Rodriguez, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-10)
ENG-520318: Replace synchronized KV cache eviction with randomized jitter and backoff to avoid coordinated eviction storms (owner: Mei Tan, estimate: 3, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-520319: Add chaos test in CI to simulate skewed arrival patterns and long-request dominance (owner: Ezra Kaplan, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-520320: Run canary rollout with per-tenant conservative policies and monitor tail-latency for 72h before full rollout (owner: SRE team, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-25)
ENG-520321: Update runtime-1.20 release notes and include guidance for tuning batching thresholds (owner: Docs, estimate: 1, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-520322: Postmortem writeup and customer impact communication draft for affected accounts (owner: Ava Martinez, estimate: 2, due: 2026-03-09)
